author: Computational Linguist
purpose: Shared ground-truth fixture for the stance-polarity-inversion bundle (epic t/2743). Consumed by the summary-pipeline gate (t/2739), the shared directional-agreement gate (t/2744), and the V-surface remediations (V1/V2 t/2745, V3/V4/V5 t/2746). Pins the observed origin inversion, the empirically-confirmed correct disposition (unmap + taxonomy gap), and the node_prop-richness requirement on the NLI gate (see nli_probe — the gate's recall depends on a contrastive label+Core node_prop, NOT on POV framing). Do NOT fork per-consumer copies — extend this file. **See `t4593_nli_label_rotation_correction` below (2026-10-28): the NLI engine's column-label mapping was rotated (t/4572) from this fixture's creation until that fix landed. The nli_probe values in empirical_findings, and the observed_deberta values in case_4/case_5, were recorded under the ROTATED (wrong) labels. Re-run under the corrected engine, several directions FLIP — most notably case_1's node-richness finding REVERSES (bare now catches, rich now misses — the opposite of this file's own `requirement` field below). Old values are kept for history, not deleted; do not read them as current.**
defect_class: A key point (or claim) that asserts the NEGATION of a taxonomy node's proposition embeds NEAR that node (cosine of a proposition and its negation is HIGH — shared content words), is selected by similarity, and is assigned/assumed 'aligned' with no direction (assert-P vs assert-not-P) check. All similarity-based gates false-green it.
contrast_with_saf_167_repro: saf-167-repro/case_1 was a LOW-retrieval-confidence miss: the wrong node was ABSENT from the key_point's bi-encoder top-80, so the t/2288 confidence gate FLAGS it. This case is the opposite and harder: the wrong node is the TOP topical match at HIGH confidence (0.7133 >> 0.45 gate) precisely BECAUSE it is the negation — topically near-identical. The confidence gate, the M5 top-3 pass, and the excludes-veto ALL pass it. Only a directional (NLI/entailment) signal catches it. That is why this bundle needs a new gate (t/2744), not a threshold tweak.

t4593_nli_label_rotation_correction.root_cause: t/4572 — scripts/embed_taxonomy.py's _classify_pairs_nli assumed raw NLI column order [entailment, neutral, contradiction]; the real cross-encoder/nli-deberta-v3-small checkpoint's config.id2label order is [contradiction, entailment, neutral]. Fixed (cb1eb8c5) to read the order from config.id2label, never assume it. Margin values (best-minus-second raw score) are unaffected by the bug -- only which semantic label was attached to the winning column was wrong. Rotation: old-reported 'entailment' -> true 'contradiction'; old-reported 'neutral' -> true 'entailment'; old-reported 'contradiction' -> true 'neutral'.
t4593_nli_label_rotation_correction.method: Re-ran the SAME stored fixture texts (not paraphrases) through the now-fixed scripts/embed_taxonomy.py._classify_pairs_nli, via _load_nli_model (reads the real model's config.id2label, no hand-rotation). research/comp-linguist/analyses/t4593-nli-rotation/rerun_cases.py.

case_1_controlled_2x2_CORRECTED.conclusion: Framing is still INERT (framed ~= no_framing on both arms, confirming the original framing-inertness finding survives the rotation). The RICHNESS finding REVERSES: under the OLD (buggy) labels, rich->contradiction(opposes, catches) and bare->entailment(agrees, misses) -- this file's own `requirement` field below, and the LIVE `nliDirectionGate.ts` node_prop construction (grep-confirmed 'label — Core', 2026-10-28), both encode that OLD direction. Under CORRECTED labels, it is now bare->contradiction(opposes, CATCHES) and rich->neutral(unrelated, MISSES) -- the opposite of what the shipped gate currently builds.
case_1_controlled_2x2_CORRECTED.caveat: This is n=1 (one claim, one node pair) both before and after the fix -- the ORIGINAL 'richness' requirement was already a single-example-derived MUST-use rule baked into V1-V5 node_prop construction (CL caution, t/4572#5: 'on n=1 it now looks counterproductive'). Do NOT flip production node_prop construction on this single reversed data point either -- same n=1 problem, opposite direction. This re-test puts the reversal on record (t/4572#5's ask); a proper small multi-example study is the right next step before touching `nliDirectionGate.ts` / V1 PS / the t/2746 requirement. Flagged to TL/PowerShell on t/4593, not actioned here.

case_4_CORRECTED.finding: The OLD fixture recorded this pair as opposes@7.51 (the t/2896 production false-demote). Under corrected labels it reads NEUTRAL (~7.44, same raw margin as before -- only the label changed) -- i.e. the gate would NOT have falsely fired on this pair under the corrected engine. The t/2896 false-demote bug and the t/4572 label-rotation bug were very likely the SAME bug: this specific false-positive resolves as a side effect of the t/4572 fix, independent of any judge-stage mitigation. Matches `correct_stance: aligned` / `MUST_NOT_FLIP` -- deberta alone now gets this arm right.

acc_127_matching_pole.finding: OLD fixture recorded opposes@1.61 (false positive) on this pole. Under corrected labels, BOTH reps read neutral -- no false fire. Matches `correct_stance: aligned` / `MUST_NOT_FLIP`.

acc_047_opposite_pole.finding: OLD fixture recorded the inversion firing via VERBATIM@4.91 (opposes) with canonical reading agrees@5.08 (missed). Under corrected labels this SWAPS: canonical now fires (contradiction@7.11, well clear of tau_contra=1.0) and verbatim now reads neutral (misses). The true inversion is still caught overall -- but only because the gate is opposes-if-any across {verbatim, canonical, attribution_text} (t/2744#10). If the engine only ran verbatim, it would now MISS this inversion it used to catch. The multi-rep contract is MORE load-bearing post-fix, not less.

case_5_CORRECTED.key_finding_CORRECTED: The original t/2900 'deberta cannot discriminate poles' finding (fires opposes on BOTH poles) does NOT hold under corrected labels: the matching pole (acc-127) reads neutral on every rep (no false fire at all), and the opposite pole (acc-047) correctly reads contradiction via canonical. Deberta alone -- no LLM-judge stage needed -- gets both arms of THIS pair right post-fix. This does not retire the LLM-judge stage in general (t/2900's judge-architecture serves other cases too, and this is still n=1), but the specific 'pole confusion' example that motivated it is resolved by the label fix, consistent with t/4572#5's prior note ('t/2900 can't-discriminate-poles finding also inverted').

empirical_findings.run_metadata: model_info: model=gemini-3.5-flash-lite, temperature=0.1, extraction_mode=fire (all_confident, 0 iterations), taxonomy_filter=rag, taxonomy_nodes=40 (doc-level RAG). acc-intentions-047 entered the 40-node candidate set on topic overlap (AI + privacy + law), then the LLM free-SELECTED it and assigned stance=aligned. This is an LLM-selection + stance-polarity error, and NOT a retrieval-confidence miss (confidence was high) nor an excludes-boundary case.
empirical_findings.taxonomy_gap_confirmed: Searched acc/saf/skp taxonomy for an anti-exceptionalism / 'adapt existing law to AI' counterpart node (terms: adapt+law, existing law, exceptionalism, ordinary+law). NONE exists — acc-intentions-047 (the 'new laws' pole) is the only near node. The correct positive home does not exist in the taxonomy; hence disposition = unmap + taxonomy gap (see t/2740).

nli_probe.finding: CORRECTED (t/2744#7, verified against the shipped scripts/nli_classify.py). The lever is node-proposition RICHNESS, NOT POV framing. A controlled 2x2 on the origin claim shows framing is INERT; the node's contrastive label+Core ('...Not Adapted Old Ones... rather than adapted existing laws') is what flips the verdict. The earlier 'framing-sensitivity' reading was CONFOUNDED — the two original probes differed in both framing AND node richness, so the flip was mis-attributed to framing.

nli_probe.requirement: judgeDirection node_prop MUST be 'label — Core' (description with the Encompasses:/Excludes: tail stripped; label-only fallback), IDENTICAL across PS (V1/V2) and TS (V3/V4/V5) so every surface feeds the engine the same text (TL cross-surface ruling). The POV-framing wrapper is retained but is NOT the safeguard. Passing label-only or a terse/bare node_prop causes MISSED inversions.
nli_probe.recall_limitation: SUPERSEDED (CL t/2756#1): the origin miss is NOT terse node text — acc-047's stored label+Core already fires opposes (verbatim margin 5.22, canonical 1.42). The recall lever is CLAIM-FIELD choice: attribution_text false-ENTAILS here while verbatim/canonical catch it (opposite of #1184). DO NOT enrich node descriptions to raise recall — tested counterproductive: a longer, more-explicit acc-047 Core NEUTRALIZED the working canonical contradiction (verbose text dilutes the NLI signal). Correct lever: run the gate over multiple claim fields, opposes-if-any (t/2744#10, implemented t/2757). Every failure mode here is false-ENTAIL (kept), never false-oppose — safe under opposes-only.

acc-intentions-047.label: Argue That AI Requires Entirely New Laws, Not Adapted Old Ones
acc-intentions-047.in_scope_core: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that asserts emerging technologies are so transformative they require entirely new legal frameworks rather than adapted existing laws. Proponents use this to justify sweeping regulatory changes tailored specifically for novel AI capabilities. Encompasses: bespoke AI legislation, regulatory sandboxes.
acc-intentions-047.excludes_clause: general arguments that caution hinders advancement or critiques of regulatory institutional inertia.
acc-intentions-047.note: The node asserts the 'new laws, NOT adapted old ones' pole. The observed source argues the exact opposite (no AI exceptionalism; existing law applies). The excludes_clause names sibling topics, NOT the negation — which is why the t/2286 excludes-veto (a sibling-topic test) cannot catch this inversion.

correct_counterpart_node.note: No positive 'adapt existing law to AI / anti-exceptionalism' accelerationist Intention node exists. Proposing one is t/2740. Until it lands, the correct disposition is unmap + unmapped_concept.

saf-beliefs-017.label: AI Deployment Speed Erodes Organizational Visibility and Control
saf-beliefs-017.in_scope_core: A Belief within safetyist discourse that describes how the rapid adoption of AI systems undermines security governance by creating a systemic loss of visibility and control over data.
saf-beliefs-017.note: t/2900 case_4: the agency→loss shape. A key_point that ASSERTS this belief (AI acts across blurred boundaries → loss of control) is a genuine AGREEMENT, but deberta reads the agency/capability language as CONTRADICTING the loss-of-control proposition — it cannot infer AI-gains-agency ⊨ humans-lose-oversight. This is the dominant safetyist/skeptic false-demote shape.

acc-intentions-127.label: Argue That Existing Laws Already Govern AI, Requiring No New AI-Specific Statutes
acc-intentions-127.in_scope_core: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that asserts AI is not legally exceptional — existing, technology-neutral bodies of law already reach AI's harms and capabilities, so bespoke AI-specific legislation is unnecessary.
acc-intentions-127.note: t/2900 case_5: the MATCHING pole of the anti-exceptionalism claim. The claim AGREES with acc-127 (both: existing law governs AI, no new statutes) — correct = no-flip — yet deberta returns opposes @ 1.61. Paired with acc-intentions-047 (the OPPOSITE pole, correct = flip) this is the pole-discrimination pair: deberta says opposes for BOTH poles of the same claim; only a reasoning judge tells agreement from opposition.

stored_key_point.verbatim: AI presents new privacy challenges, but treating AI as if it lives outside the parameters of ordinary privacy law is fallacious. The emerging lesson from privacy regulators and enforcers is increasingly clear: there is no AI exceptionalism. The same principles that have long governed responsible data use still apply. What changes is where those principles need to be built.
